thread:
maya: FYI — noticing a p99 TTFT spike in us-west starting ~07:12 UTC. p50/p95 basically stable, p99 jumped from ~320ms to ~1.2s. tokens/sec on the top-level dashboard doesn't correlate (no obvious capacity drop). https://grafana.redwood.test/d/abc123/token-observability?orgId=1 :eyes:

aj: Can you paste the panel/time range and a sample PromQL you used? Also which model_family is the worst?

maya: Panel: last 30m, grouped by model_family and instance. Quick PromQL I used:```
# tokens/sec by instance + model
sum by (instance, model_family) (rate(tokens_served_total[1m]))

# p99 TTFT by instance + model
histogram_quantile(0.99, sum(rate(token_latency_seconds_bucket[5m])) by (le, instance, model_family))

# TTFT summary metric (fallback)
max by(instance, model_family) (ttft_seconds{job="inference"})
```
The biggest offenders look like `gptx-3` running 8-bit quant on a few old p2-equivalent nodes.

infra-bot: [ALERT] token_ttft_p99_high: firing (us-west). Started 2026-03-18T07:13:05Z. Current p99 ~1.18s (threshold 0.8s). Alert grouped by model_family=gptx-3, instance=i-0a4b.

ravi: Two quick checks: 1) KV cache hit ratio — if misses go up, TTFT jumps because of full KV recompute. Try:```
sum by(instance, model_family) (rate(kv_cache_hit_total[5m])) / sum by(instance, model_family) (rate(kv_cache_request_total[5m]))
```
2) Per-instance tokens in-flight / per-gpu queuing:```
sum by(instance) (inflight_tokens{job="serving"}) / on(instance) group_left() (gpu_count{job="node_inventory"})
```

lin: We're also seeing a handful of long-context requests from a customer in us-west (label: tenant=acme-ux) that started at ~07:10. Those add big prefix tokens and blow up p99 without changing tokens/sec much. Would like to segment by tenant on the dashboard.

maya: Good catch @lin — can you dump a few sample request_ids from logs? If it's a single tenant spamming long contexts we can route them to a dedicated burst pool.

lin: grabbing sample IDs now — putting 3 into the thread: `req_20260318_070937_a1`, `req_20260318_071042_b2`, `req_20260318_071115_c9`. Logs show context lengths ~80k tokens for two of them.

aj: Routing option is reasonable short-term. Long-term we should: 1) add a tokens_per_gpu panel (tokens served / gpu_count) 2) add a p99 alert that is conditional on tokens_per_gpu < X (to avoid false positives when overloaded) 3) add tenant-level rate limit guard for extreme contexts. I'll take the Grafana panel.

maya: Also, cost note — long-context bursts increase per-request token cost and can spike throughput consumption. If we move them to a dedicated pool we can charge them or apply throttles. Need a short postmortem note in incidents if we route.

aj: I'll add a dashboard panel and an alert tweak. Proposed queries:```
# tokens per GPU (1m avg)
(sum by(region) (rate(tokens_served_total[1m])) ) / sum by(region) (gpu_count)
```
Add a grafana stat with a 5m rolling avg. Proposed alert: fire when p99 TTFT > 900ms AND tokens_per_gpu < 3000 (to catch tail issues, not overload).

ops-runbook-bot: Runbook: https://runbooks.redwood.test/ttft-p99-tailburst — includes mitigation steps: 1) identify tenant via request_id, 2) temporarily pin tenant to burst pool, 3) enable per-tenant context cap, 4) notify account team.

ravi: One more: tune the token_latency histogram buckets to have tighter bins under 1s so p95/p99 are more actionable. Current buckets are too coarse (0.5s, 1s, 2s).

maya: Agreed. @aj can you also add a small panel showing KV-cache hit ratio alongside p99 so on-call can triage faster?

aj: Yep. Will push a patch to the grafana repo (`infra/grafana/dashboards/token_observability.json`) in ~20m, and create an alert PR to change the threshold and add the tokens_per_gpu condition.

lin: If we route those tenants, we should include a soft limit and a warning webhook so customers get visibility before throttles.

maya: OK — plan: aj pushes panels/alerts, lin prepares tenant routing plan + webhook message, ravi tweaks histogram buckets, ops-runbook-bot runbook linked. If anyone hits anything else ping here. :thumbsup:

infra-bot: Note: creating incident CR to track mitigation: INC-20260318-042.

maya: Thanks everyone. I'll follow up with a quick incident note once routing decision is made. :memo:
